extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants and their attorneys/agents seeking special or accelerated examination with the USPTO
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for petitioning the USPTO to accord a patent application "special" status (including prioritized/accelerated examination) and the procedural/substantive prerequisites for participation and prosecution under those programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special status for environmental-quality inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO will accord "special" status to patent applications for inventions which materially enhance the quality of the environment by contributing to the restoration or maintenance of air, water, and soil.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition under 37 CFR 1.102 must state that special status is sought because the invention materially enhances environmental quality; no fee required. If the disclosure is not clear on its face, the petition must be accompanied by a statement under 37 CFR 1.102 explaining how the materiality standard is met. Materiality cannot be mere speculation about hypothetical end-user applications nor be satisfied by a minor aspect of the claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special status for energy-related inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO will accord "special" status to patent applications for inventions which materially contribute to (A) discovery/development of energy resources or (B) more efficient utilization and conservation of energy resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples for (A) include fossil fuels, hydrogen, nuclear, solar; (B) includes inventions reducing energy consumption in combustion systems, industrial equipment, household appliances. Petition under 37 CFR 1.102 must state how the invention materially contributes to category (A) or (B); no fee required. If not clear on the face, petition must include a statement under 37 CFR 1.102 explaining how materiality is met. Materiality cannot be speculative or rely on minor aspects of the claimed invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special status for inventions relating to recombinant DNA (safety)
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO will accord "special" status to patent applications relating to safety of research in the field of recombinant DNA upon appropriate petition and payment of the fee under 37 CFR 1.17(h).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions should be accompanied by statements under 37 CFR 1.102 by applicant/assignee/registered practitioner explaining the relationship of the invention to recombinant DNA research safety. Fee under 37 CFR 1.17(h) must also be paid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special status for superconductivity inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO will, on request, accord "special" status to patent applications for inventions involving superconductivity materials (materials, manufacture, application).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request should be accompanied by a statement under 37 CFR 1.102 that the invention involves superconductive materials. No fee required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special status for HIV/AIDS and cancer inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO will accord "special" status to patent applications relating to HIV/AIDS and cancer to encourage prompt disclosure of advances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants seeking special status should file a petition and the fee under 37 CFR 1.17(h). The petition should be accompanied by a statement explaining how the invention contributes to diagnosis, treatment, or prevention of HIV/AIDS or cancer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special status for inventions countering terrorism
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO will accord "special" status to patent applications for inventions which materially contribute to countering terrorism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition under 37 CFR 1.102 must state that special status is sought because the invention materially contributes to countering terrorism; no fee required. If the application disclosure is not clear, petition must include a statement under 37 CFR 1.102 explaining materiality. Materiality does not permit speculation about hypothetical end-user application nor reliance on minor aspects of the claimed invention. Examples of technologies may include detecting/identifying explosives, aircraft sensors/security systems, vehicular barricades/disabling systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special status for biotechnology applications by small entities
rubrics_metrics.description: Small-entity applicants may request that their biotechnology applications be granted "special" status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition (with fee under 37 CFR 1.17(h)) must: (A) state or establish small entity status; (B) state that the subject of the patent application is a major asset of the small entity; and (C) state that development of the technology will be significantly impaired if examination is delayed, with an explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal requirements of any petition to make special
rubrics_metrics.description: Any petition to make special should be in writing and identify the application by application number and filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions should follow these minimal formalities to be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling and recordation of petitions to make special
rubrics_metrics.description: Each petition to make special, regardless of ground, is made of record in the application file together with the decision; petitions and decisions receive paper numbers and are entered in the file contents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical support staff ensure prior papers are entered before forwarding for consideration. Petitions are decided by the Special Program Examiner of the assigned Technology Center. Applications made special are advanced out of turn and treated as special throughout prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special examining procedure (legacy accelerated exam) prerequisites (A–E)
rubrics_metrics.description: A new application may be granted special status (legacy special examining procedure) if: (A) petition with fee under 37 CFR 1.17(h); (B) presents all claims directed to a single invention or will make an election without traverse; (C) submits statement that a pre-examination search was made listing field(s) of search; (D) submits copies of closest references not of record; and (E) submits a detailed discussion of references per 37 CFR 1.111(b) and (c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If requirements not met, applicant is notified and given one opportunity to perfect via renewed petition; divisional applications must meet requirements on their own; refusal to elect without traverse will result in denial and application awaiting regular turn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accelerated examination eligibility (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: A new application may be granted accelerated examination status if it meets the comprehensive requirements set out in subsection I (items A–I) for petitions filed on or after August 25, 2006.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications filed prior to Aug 25, 2006 are not eligible for this program except for health/age or PPH. For prioritized examination under 37 CFR 1.102(e) see MPEP § 708.02(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Accelerated exam requirement: petition and fee or qualifying subject-matter statement (I(A))
rubrics_metrics.description: The application must be filed with a petition to make special under the accelerated examination program accompanied by either the fee under 37 CFR 1.17(h) or a statement that the claimed subject matter is directed to environmental quality, energy development/conservation, or countering terrorism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant should use form PTO/SB/28 for filing the petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accelerated exam requirement: application type (I(B))
rubrics_metrics.description: The application must be a non-reissue utility or design application filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain categories are excluded (see eligibility).

rubrics_metrics.name: Accelerated exam requirement: electronic filing (I(C))
rubrics_metrics.description: The application, petition, and required fees must be filed electronically using the USPTO’s EFS or EFS-Web (unless those systems are unavailable during normal business hours at the time of filing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If EFS/EFS-Web unavailable and filing is by mail with a statement explaining the unavailability, the final disposition may occur later than twelve months from filing. See VIII.F for more.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accelerated exam requirement: application must be complete and in condition for examination (I(D))
rubrics_metrics.description: At filing the application must be complete under 37 CFR 1.51 and in condition for examination (e.g., filed with basic filing fee, search fee, examination fee, application size fee if applicable, and an executed oath or declaration under 37 CFR 1.63).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications not in condition for examination cannot be perfected for accelerated status via the one-time cure opportunity described in subsection II.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim limits for accelerated examination (I(E))
rubrics_metrics.description: Application must contain three or fewer independent claims and twenty or fewer total claims; must not contain any multiple dependent claims. By filing petition, applicant agrees not to separately argue the patentability of any dependent claim during any appeal in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition must include a statement that applicant will agree not to separately argue dependent claims on appeal (form PTO/SB/28).

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-invention requirement and election without traverse (I(F))
rubrics_metrics.description: The claims must be directed to a single invention. If USPTO determines claims are not directed to a single invention, applicant must make an election without traverse in a telephonic interview; petition must include statement agreeing to such election.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant refuses to elect without traverse, petition will be denied; telephone restriction practice will be followed; election may be made at time of filing petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview willingness requirement (I(G))
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant must be willing to have an interview (including before a first Office action) to discuss prior art and potential rejections/objections with the intention of clarifying and resolving issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition must include a statement that applicant will agree to have such an interview when requested by the examiner (form PTO/SB/28).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preexamination search requirements (I(H))
rubrics_metrics.description: At filing applicant must provide a statement that a preexamination search was conducted, identifying field of search by U.S. class/subclass and date; for database searches include search logic/chemical structure/sequence used, file name(s), database service, and date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search must involve U.S. patents and patent application publications, foreign patent documents, and non-patent literature unless applicant justifies with reasonable certainty that no more pertinent references would be found in an eliminated source. Search must be directed to the claimed invention, encompass all claim features (broadest reasonable interpretation), and also encompass disclosed features that may be claimed. A foreign patent office search report will not satisfy this requirement unless it meets the preexamination search requirements. Statements supporting the petition must be made in good faith (see 37 CFR 1.56 and 10.18).

rubrics_metrics.name: Accelerated examination support document requirements (I(I) items 1–6)
rubrics_metrics.description: At filing applicant must provide an accelerated examination support document (AESD) that: (1) includes an IDS compliant with 37 CFR 1.98 citing each reference deemed most closely related to subject matter of each claim; (2) for each cited reference, identifies all claim limitations disclosed by the reference and where disclosed; (3) includes a detailed explanation of how each claim is patentable over cited references with the particularity required by 37 CFR 1.111(b) and (c); (4) includes a concise statement of utility of the invention as defined in each independent claim (unless design application); (5) shows where each claim limitation finds support under first paragraph of 35 U.S.C. 112 in the written description (and in any priority applications); and (6) identifies any cited references that may be disqualified as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 103(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An AESD that fails to encompass amended/new claims will render those amendments not fully responsive and not entered. IDS filed with an updated AESD must comply with 37 CFR 1.97 and 1.98.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision and single-opportunity to perfect defective petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: If petition/accelerated examination support document does not meet requirements (including insufficient search), applicant will be notified of defects and given a single opportunity to perfect the petition/AESD within one month (no extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This opportunity does not apply to applications not in condition for examination at filing. If corrected timely, petition will be granted, but final disposition may occur later than twelve months from filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial examiner action timing and interview-first practice (III)
rubrics_metrics.description: Once granted special status the application will be docketed and taken up expeditiously (e.g., within two weeks). If an examiner determines an issue must be addressed, the examiner will telephone the applicant to discuss amendments/submissions prior to issuing an Office action. The USPTO will not issue an Office action (other than notice of allowance) unless: (A) an interview was conducted but did not result in allowance, or (B) a determination is made that an interview is unlikely to result in allowance. Prior to mailing any Office action rejecting claims, the USPTO will conduct a conference to review the rejections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Telephone restriction practice applies if claims not to single invention; applicant must make election without traverse in telephonic interview. If an Office action other than allowance or final is mailed, it will set a shortened statutory period of one month (30 days or longer) with no extensions; failure to timely reply results in abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply limitations and amendment entry rules (IV)
rubrics_metrics.description: A reply to an Office action must be limited to the rejections, objections, and requirements made. Any amendment that would (A) add claims resulting in more than three independent claims or more than twenty total claims; (B) present claims not encompassed by the preexamination search or an updated AESD; or (C) present claims directed to a non-elected invention or an invention other than previously claimed will be treated as not fully responsive and will not be entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For any amendment to claims not encompassed by the AESD, applicant must provide an updated AESD that encompasses the amended/new claims at time of filing; failure to do so causes the amendment to be not entered. All replies/papers must be filed electronically via EFS-Web; if not, final disposition may occur later than 12 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-allowance processing requirements (V)
rubrics_metrics.description: The mailing of a notice of allowance is the final disposition for the 12-month goal. In response applicant must pay the issue fee within three months from mailing of the Notice of Allowance and Fee(s) Due (form PTOL-85) to avoid abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To be expeditiously issued as a patent applicant must: (A) pay the issue fee (and any outstanding fees) within one month from the mailing date of PTOL-85; and (B) not file any post-allowance papers that are not required by the USPTO (e.g., unsolicited 37 CFR 1.312 amendments).

rubrics_metrics.name: After-final and appeal procedures as final dispositions (VI)
rubrics_metrics.description: The mailing of a final Office action or the filing of a notice of appeal, whichever is earlier, is the final disposition for the 12-month goal. For expedited forwarding to the Board (BPAI) applicant must promptly file the notice of appeal, appeal brief, and appeal fees and must not request a pre-appeal brief conference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A pre-appeal brief conference is not useful because the examiner will have already conducted the required conference prior to mailing the final Office action. Filing an RCE under 37 CFR 1.114 with submission and fee is a final disposition for the 12-month goal; application retains special status and the goal becomes reaching final disposition within 12 months from the RCE filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proceedings outside normal examination suspend acceleration (VII)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application becomes involved in proceedings outside the normal examination process (secrecy order, national security review, interference, petitions under 37 CFR 1.181–1.183, etc.), the application will be treated as special but will not be accelerated during those proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once such proceedings are completed, the USPTO will process the application expeditiously under the accelerated program until final disposition, but that may occur later than twelve months from filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility exclusions for accelerated examination (VIII.A)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain filings are not eligible for the accelerated examination program: (1) plant applications; (2) reissue applications; (3) applications entering national stage after compliance with 35 U.S.C. 371; (4) reexamination proceedings; (5) RCEs under 37 CFR 1.114 (unless application was previously granted special status under the program); and (6) petitions to make special based on applicant's health or age or under the PPH pilot program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design patent applicants may instead use the expedited examination program per MPEP § 1504.30 and 37 CFR 1.155.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form to use for petitions (VIII.B)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant should use form PTO/SB/28 for filing a petition to make special (other than those based on health/age or PPH pilot).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form is available on EFS-Web and the USPTO website; see URL provided in MPEP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for examination (VIII.C beginning)
rubrics_metrics.description: The application must be in condition for examination at filing, meaning it must include required fees and executed oath/declaration: basic filing fee, search fee, and examination fee under 37 CFR 1.16, application size fee if applicable, and an executed oath or declaration under 37 CFR 1.63.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to file a complete application in condition for examination precludes eligibility/perfection for accelerated examination.
